newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU proposal to allow beef labelling blocked.
newsitem.headline: EU proposal to allow beef labelling blocked.

text.p: A proposal by European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler for beef to be labelled to restore market confidence has been blocked for a second time, a Commission official said on Friday.
"The proposal which is to be agreed by what is known as a written proceedure has been blocked on a small technical point. It is expected to be agreed next week," the official said.

A Commission source told Reuters that Science Commissioner Edith Cresson had asked for the proposal, which includes new regulations creating an identification system for bovine animals to include the use of electronic chip technology.
"Commissioner Cresson has asked for the proposal to be amended to include the use of micro-chips which can be embedded under an animals skin to reduce the possiblity of fraud," the source said.
Earlier the written procedure, which allows Commissioners to agree without debate, was blocked on another technicality by Industry Commissioner for Martin Bangemann.
The draft proposal, which must be approved by farm ministers aims to restore public confidence in beef and beef products by allowing labelling under a voluntary scheme.
All cows will have to be registered on computers and will be tagged from birth. The current proposal specifies a tag in each ear.
Those wishing to label beef and beef products will have to comply with a mandatory list of descriptions restricting what can be said about a product.
Commissioner Fischler is proposing two separate measures.
The first builds on existing legislation to require all animals to wear a tag in each ear, to be given passports and to be registered on central computers, the document says.
The identification system is linked to a labelling scheme for beef and beef products so that the origins of all meat can be checked.
Operators and organisations marketing beef will be allowed to label their products according to strict, mandatory rules.

Labels will only be allowed to describe the country or national region of origin, gender and method of fattening . The proposal does not oblige operators or organisations to label beef but if they choose to do so they will be obliged to stay within the boundaries of the legislation.
